title: [kube] Add "podman container inspect" field to help distinguish init containers
body:
### Feature request description

Hi,

I use `podman kube play` extensively.
I also use `podman events` with custom scripts to react to some container events.

Recently I've been trying to execute some commands when a container exits cleanly. However I need init containers to be excluded from that logic. This has proven difficult because I could not find a way to distinguish init containers from regular ones when using `podman container inspect <cntID>`.

### Suggest potential solution

Introduce a new field inside `podman container inspect` that indicates whether the container refers to an init container or not.

### Have you considered any alternatives?

I can flag init containers manually by using annotations (e.g. `com.example.init-container/mycontainer`), then when a container exits, I can check whether such an annotation exists for the container.
This is tedious and error prone, so I would prefer a native solution.

Alternatively, I've tried parsing the YAML file that was used to start the pod, but this is also error prone (and introduces a TOCTOU race condition because the file may have beeen altered between the time the `podman play kube` command was run and the time my script parses the file).

### Additional context

```sh
$ uname -a
Linux localhost 6.19.14-108.fc42.x86_64 #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Thu May 21 18:06:59 UTC 2026 x86_64 GNU/Linux

$ podman version
Client:        Podman Engine
Version:       5.8.2
API Version:   5.8.2
Go Version:    go1.25.8 X:nodwarf5
Git Commit:    5b263b5f5b48004a87caac44e67349a8266d9ef4
Built:         Tue Apr 14 02:00:00 2026
Build Origin:  Fedora Project
OS/Arch:       linux/amd64
```

comments.body: Hi! I’m currently working on this issue. I’ve reproduced it and identified the missing init-container field in `podman container inspect`. I’m working on the fix and tests.
